questions.question_text: Which expression represents the full expansion of $(x+3)^{4}$?

options.why: Multiplied each binomial coefficient by $3$ every time instead of by the power $3^{r}$.

options.why: Multiplied $6 \times 4 = 24$ instead of squaring the $4x$ term to get $6 \times 16 = 96$.
Omitted the binomial coefficients $^{4}C_{1} = 4$ and $^{4}C_{2} = 6$.

questions.question_text: Find the coefficient of $x^{2}$ in the expansion of $(2+3x)(1+2x)^{4}$.

options.why: Only multiplied $2 \times 24 = 48$, missing the linear cross term $3x \times 8x = 24x^{2}$.
Took the coefficient of $x^{2}$ directly from $(1+2x)^{4}$ without expanding the outer factor.
Double counted the linear contribution, adding $48 + 48 = 96$.
